title: TSM Earnings Tomorrow: Can Strong AI Demand Boost Q3 Results?
author: Na
description: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) is set to report Q3 2026 results with expected revenues of $45.62 billion, up 37.8% year-over-year, driven by robust AI chip demand and advanced process technologies. The company raised 2026 capex guidance to $60-$64 billion, though margin pressure from 2nm expansion and overseas facilities is anticipated. Despite a Zacks Rank #1 rating, TSMC carries a negative Earnings ESP of -0.67%, warranting caution ahead of results.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong year-over-year revenue growth (37.8%), robust AI-driven demand, industry-leading process technologies, consistent earnings beats, and Zacks Rank #1 rating support positive outlook. However, negative Earnings ESP (-0.67%) and margin pressure from capex investments introduce some caution.
Intel shows modest growth with 25% YoY revenue increase in Q2 2026 and 31% growth in foundry operations, but lags TSMC's momentum. Positioned as a competitor but without the same AI-driven tailwinds.
Exceptional performance with 86% YoY revenue growth and 221% surge in AI semiconductor revenues demonstrates strong positioning in the AI chip market, outpacing broader semiconductor growth.

title: Applied Materials vs. Intel: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Mike Schwenk
description: Applied Materials and Intel represent different points in the semiconductor supply chain. Applied Materials reported strong fiscal 2025 results with $28.4B revenue, 24.7% net margin, and $5.7B free cash flow, with Q3 2026 showing 25% revenue growth. Intel faced challenges with negative free cash flow in 2025, a $12.5B noncash charge in Q2 2026, and significant shareholder dilution from $23B in new stock sales. The analyst favors Applied Materials as the better buy but recommends dollar-cost averaging due to cyclical industry risks, while Intel's turnaround depends on its unprofitable foundry business becoming profitable.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong financial performance with 24.7% net margin, $5.7B free cash flow in fiscal 2025, and 25% revenue growth in latest quarter. Analyst recommends it as the better buy despite cyclical risks and China exposure concerns.

Negative free cash flow of $4.9B in 2025, unprofitable foundry business, $12.5B noncash charge in Q2 2026, and significant shareholder dilution from $23B stock sale in August 2026. Turnaround remains uncertain and dependent on foundry profitability.

title: As Big Tech Designs Its Own AI Chips, the Companies Behind the Scenes Win
author: Chris Neiger
description: As major tech companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon develop custom AI processors instead of relying solely on GPUs, semiconductor designers and manufacturers are positioned to benefit significantly. Custom processors are growing 45% annually compared to 16% for GPUs, with companies like Broadcom, Marvell, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing capturing substantial market share and revenue growth.

title: Prediction: $5,000 Invested in Taiwan Semiconductor Could Be Worth This Much by 2030
author: Stefon Walters
description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is positioned for strong growth through 2030, with analyst predictions suggesting a $5,000 investment could grow to $8,000. TSMC's virtual monopoly on advanced AI chip manufacturing, commanding 73% of the foundry market and over 95% of advanced AI chips, combined with expanding profit margins and consistent earnings growth, supports the bullish outlook. The company's dominance in supplying chips to major AI hyperscalers provides a lucrative position regardless of which company leads the AI race.

The analyst predicts 60% returns by 2030 based on feasible 15.6% annual EPS growth, supported by ongoing AI infrastructure buildout.

title: Applied Materials vs. Advanced Micro Devices: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares Applied Materials, which manufactures semiconductor equipment, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), which designs high-performance processors. While both benefit from AI demand, AMD is recommended as the better buy due to its direct competition in the AI chip market, six consecutive quarters of above-30% growth, and strategic partnerships with major AI companies. Applied Materials is viewed as a solid diversified play but lacks AMD's central position in the AI boom.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Described as a well-run business with healthy orders and positive outlook, but faces headwinds including high customer concentration, export control risks, and a $252 million settlement. Trades at lower valuation multiples but lacks direct exposure to the core AI chip market.

Recommended as the clear winner with six consecutive quarters of above-30% growth, doubled data center revenue in Q2 2026, strategic partnerships with OpenAI and Anthropic, and positioned as the primary alternative to Nvidia in the AI chip market. Directly competing for the biggest prize in semiconductors.
